items.q: Five students reported how many hours they slept the night before a test: 4, 7, 5, 8 and 6. What is the mean number of hours?

mistakes.why: 30 is the total. The mean divides the total by the number of values, 5.
5 is the third number as listed, not the mean. Add all five values and divide by 5.

items.q: In a memory test, five participants recalled 3, 9, 4, 15 and 7 words. What is the median number of words recalled?

why.correct: In order: 3, 4, 7, 9, 15. The middle (third) value is 7.

mistakes.why: 4 is the middle of the list as written. Put the values in order first: 3, 4, 7, 9, 15.
7.6 is the mean. The median is the middle value once the list is in order.

items.q: Six children took 2, 5, 6, 9, 11 and 13 minutes to solve a puzzle. What is the median time, in minutes?

why.correct: With six values, the median is halfway between the two middle values: $\frac{6 + 9}{2} = 7.5$ minutes.

mistakes.why: 6 is only the lower of the two middle values. With an even count, average the two middle values, 6 and 9.
9 is only the upper of the two middle values. Average 6 and 9.

items.q: Eight people rated a movie from 1 to 10: 2, 4, 4, 7, 9, 9, 9 and 10. What is the mode?

why.correct: 9 appears three times, more than any other rating.

mistakes.why: 3 is how many times the mode appears. The mode is the value itself, 9.
8 is the median. The mode is the most frequent value.

items.q: Five drivers took 12, 5, 19, 8 and 15 seconds to notice a road sign. What is the range, in seconds?

mistakes.why: 19 is the highest value. Subtract the lowest, 5.
That subtracts the first value from the last as listed (15 - 12). Use the highest and lowest values.

items.q: Two classes both have a mean score of 75 on a test. Class A has a standard deviation of 4; Class B has a standard deviation of 15. What does this tell you?
options: Scores in Class B are more spread out from the mean
Class B scored higher on average than Class A
Class A has more students than Class B
Class B has a smaller range than Class A

why.correct: The standard deviation is roughly the typical distance of scores from the mean. A standard deviation of 15 means scores are much more spread out than with 4.
options: Right: a larger standard deviation means more variation.
Both means are 75, so neither scored higher on average.
Standard deviation measures spread, not the number of students.
A larger standard deviation usually goes with a larger range, not a smaller one.

items.q: A store reports the "average" income of its customers. A few customers are billionaires. Which measure would best describe a typical customer’s income?
options: The mean, because it uses each customer’s income
The median, because extreme values barely move it
The range, because it covers the lowest and highest incomes
The standard deviation, because it shows variation

why.correct: Outliers pull the mean toward them. In a skewed distribution, the median better describes the typical case.
options: Using every value is why the few billionaires pull it far up.
Right: the median depends on the middle, not the extremes.
The range measures spread, not a typical value.
Standard deviation measures spread, not a typical value.

items.q: Scores on a reading test cluster in two separate peaks, one around 40 and one around 80, with few scores in between. How is this distribution described?
options: Symmetric with one peak
Positively skewed
Bimodal
Negatively skewed

why.correct: A bimodal distribution has two peaks. It often means two different groups are mixed together, such as students who did and did not read the assigned book.
options: A symmetric distribution with one peak has a single hump in the middle.
Skew is one peak with a long tail on one side.
Right: two modes, two peaks.
Skew is one peak with a long tail on one side.

items.q: A researcher reports that participants’ recall scores had a mean of 12 words and a standard deviation of 0.5. What does the small standard deviation suggest?
options: The participants recalled about half a word on average
The study had a small sample of participants
The scores contained one or two extreme outliers
Most participants recalled close to 12 words

why.correct: The standard deviation measures variation. A value of 0.5 means almost everyone recalled between 11 and 13 words.
options: The mean is 12; the 0.5 describes spread around it.
Standard deviation is about spread, not sample size.
Outliers would make the standard deviation larger, not smaller.
Right: a small standard deviation means scores sit close to the mean.

items.q: What is the mean reaction time across all 10 trials, in milliseconds?

mistakes.why: That averages the four times in the table (280, 300, 320, 900) without counting how many trials had each. Multiply each time by its number of trials first.
3620 is the total of all 10 trials. Divide by 10.

items.q: What is the median reaction time, in milliseconds?

why.correct: In order: 280, 280, 300, 300, 300, 300, 320, 320, 320, 900. The two middle values (5th and 6th) are both 300, so the median is 300 ms.

mistakes.why: 362 is the mean. The median is the middle of the ordered list.
That is halfway between 300 and 320, the middle of the table’s rows. Count trials: the 5th and 6th trials in order are both 300.

items.q: Which statistic gives the better summary of this participant’s usual reaction time, and why?
options: The median, because the 900 ms sneeze trial pulls the mean up
The mean, because it uses each trial, including the 900 ms one
The range, because it shows the fastest and slowest trials
The mode and the mean are equal, so either works

why.correct: The median (300 ms) sits with the typical trials; the mean (362 ms) is higher than nine of the ten trials because of a single outlier.
options: Right: one outlier moves the mean far more than the median.
Including the outlier is exactly why the mean misleads here.
The range describes spread, not a usual value.
The mode is 300 and the mean is 362; they are not equal.

items.q: What is the range of the reaction times, in milliseconds?

mistakes.why: 40 is the range without the outlier (320 - 280). The range uses the highest value, 900.
900 is the highest value. Subtract the lowest, 280.

items.q: If the researcher drops the 900 ms trial as a recording error, what happens to the mean and the median?
options: Both drop by about the same amount
The mean drops a lot; the median stays at 300
The median drops a lot; the mean stays about the same
Neither changes, since one trial is a small part of the data

why.correct: Without the outlier, the mean is $\frac{2720}{9} \approx 302$ ms; the median of the nine remaining trials is the 5th value, 300 ms. The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is not.
options: The mean falls by about 60 ms; the median does not change.
Right: the mean falls to about 302 ms, and the middle of the nine values is still 300.
This reverses the effect: the mean is the measure sensitive to outliers.
One extreme trial changes the mean a great deal.

items.q: How is the shape of this distribution best described?
options: Positively skewed
Bimodal
Negatively skewed
Symmetric

why.correct: The tail points toward the low scores, so the distribution is negatively skewed. Easy tests often produce this shape.
options: A positive skew has its tail toward the high values; this tail points to the low scores.
There is one peak, from 80 to 90.
Right: most scores are high, with a tail stretching toward the low scores.
A symmetric distribution has matching sides; this one has a tail on the left.

items.q: In this distribution, how do the mean and median compare?
options: The mean is higher than the median
The mean and median are exactly equal
The median is lower than the mode by 30 points
The mean is lower than the median

why.correct: The mean is pulled toward the tail. With a tail of low scores (negative skew), the mean falls below the median.
options: That is the pattern for a positive skew, with a tail of high values.
They are equal in a symmetric distribution, not a skewed one.
The mode is in the 80 to 90 bin and the median is in the same region.
Right: the few low scores pull the mean down toward the tail.

items.q: Which score range holds the most students?

why.correct: The tallest bar of a histogram is the most frequent range: here 80 to 90, with 8 students.
options: Right: 8 students, the tallest bar.
That bar holds 5 students.
That bar holds 4 students.
That bar holds 1 student.
